Verdun, the Somme, Tannenberg, Caporetto. Each name on this map of World War I battles carries a number that still shocks. Here are six.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Tannenberg, 26-30 August 1914: the German 8th Army encircled and nearly destroyed the Russian 2nd Army. Its commander Samsonov disappeared into the woods and killed himself. Hindenburg picked the name to echo the 1410 defeat of the Teutonic Knights.

2/ Verdun, 21 February to 18 December 1916: about 302 days. Combined French and German casualties are estimated at roughly 714,000. Falkenhayn wanted France to 'bleed itself white'; historians debate how fixed that plan was.

3/ The Somme, 1 July to 18 November 1916: the first day cost the British Army 57,470 casualties, including 19,240 killed. Tanks made their debut on 15 September at Flers-Courcelette. The Allies advanced about 10 km.

4/ The Brusilov Offensive, 4 June to 20 September 1916: Russia's biggest success of the war. Austria-Hungary lost an estimated 616,000 men, Germany had to halt its attack at Verdun, and Romania decided to join the Entente.

5/ Caporetto, 24 October to 19 November 1917: German-backed forces drove Italy back about 150 km to the Piave. Some 265,000 to 275,000 Italians were captured. A young Erwin Rommel won the Pour le Mérite here.
6/ In Italian, 'Caporetto' now means a disastrous defeat. Italy replaced Cadorna with Armando Diaz, and the line held on the Piave.
Behind each dot on the map is a different kind of defeat. Which battle do you think changed the war most? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
